observation.visible_scene: A close-up of a single lit match held at an angle (stick pointing down-right) against a dark, featureless background. A bright yellow-white flame rises from the match head, which is ringed at its base by a small blue zone; a soft radial glow and a faint magenta lens halo surround the flame. The match is already burning at the first frame.
visible_changes: The flame is initially a tall plume that reaches the top edge of the frame (frames 1-6), then subsides to a shorter, steadier teardrop shape from about frame 7 onward, with continuous small flicker/deformation of its outline.
The match head progressively darkens/chars; a reddish-pink glow becomes more apparent around the head in the middle and later frames.
The blue flame zone at the base of the head persists throughout the excerpt.
The surrounding halo/glow shifts in prominence, appearing more diffuse and magenta-tinted in mid-to-late frames as the bright core settles.
The match stick's orientation and position within the frame stay roughly constant; the visible motion is the flame's height change and flicker, not translation of the match.
outside_clip_unknowns: The ignition moment (before t=0) is not shown; the match is already alight.
Whether the flame later dies out or the match burns down further after the last frame is not shown.
No holder, strike surface, or operator is visible.
The exact material/texture of the match head is partly obscured by the bright flame.
uncertain_details: Camera motion is hard to judge because the background is uniformly dark; the match's stable framing suggests little or no deliberate camera movement, but this cannot be confirmed.
Fine color and char detail of the match head are uncertain due to overexposure from the adjacent flame.
